fanbase.name: The Delusionals
fanbase.why: You told us people think you're a bit delusional. That's not the risk — that's the brand. Every fan you have is chasing something other people call unrealistic. Give them a name that turns the insult into a badge.

alts.w: Owns your morning moment. Softer, very ownable visually (golden hour).
From 'chasing your highest potential'. Short, chantable, works as merch.

positioning: The artist who says the *dream* out loud — then *documents* every step of making it real.

diagnostic.bottleneck: You don't have a *content* problem. You have a *format* problem.
diagnostic.detail: You have ideas, 10+ finished tracks, live footage, travel footage, Tomorrowland on your résumé and 5–10 hours a week. That's more raw material than 90% of artists. What you don't have is one repeatable format — so every post starts from zero, and starting from zero is what procrastination feeds on.
diagnostic.thesisDetail: Freedom, euphoria, 'living your life to the fullest' — every melodic artist sells that. It's invisible. What nobody else can say is: "I played Tomorrowland, and I'm telling you right now I'm going to headline it." Say it publicly, track it daily, and let people watch. The thing you think people judge you for is the only thing that makes you different.

gauges.n: Tomorrowland, LIV, a 4M-view post. Most artists would kill for this.
10+ finished unreleased tracks. You can test, not guess.
'Freedom' is true to you but generic on a feed.
No repeatable series. Every post starts from zero.
No pre-save or fan capture system mentioned.

disagreements.you: "What's holding me back is the content — my team isn't big enough."
disagreements.us: A bigger team won't fix it. With 5–10h a week you can post 4 times a week — if the format is decided before you open the camera. Procrastination isn't a discipline problem here, it's a blank-page problem. One format removes the blank page.

Your references are John Summit, Kream and Kaskade — that's house and progressive festival energy, not melodic techno. Label yourself in the lane your references live in, or the algorithm sends you to an audience that doesn't want your drops.

disagreements.you: "The hook was phenomenal — that's why it hit 4M."
disagreements.us: The hook got the stop. You also said the song was insane and the video was short. That's three variables, and you only credited one. With 10+ unreleased tracks, you should be testing songs the way you test hooks — the next 4M might be a track sitting in your vault.

disagreements.you: "I want to model Martin Garrix because he's genuine."
disagreements.us: Genuine is table stakes. What's copyable about Garrix is that people could recognise him instantly — one signature sound and one look, repeated for years. Model the signature, not the personality.

insights.d: John Summit's rise was carried as much by his story — the accountant who quit to DJ — as by his tracks. People follow a character before they follow a catalogue. Your character is already written: the guy who said he'd headline Tomorrowland.
Kaskade turned a set style into a named, recurring thing (Redux) that fans return for. A name turns a post into a series, and a series into a habit.

visualRefs.w: Golden-hour light, wind, bodies in open space — Days of Heaven, The Tree of Life.
Young, free, outdoors, sun-flared. Freedom shown, never told.
Cosmic scale against a single human. Your 'cosmic' tile, done with restraint.

higgsfield: Cinematic 9:16 vertical, golden hour over a calm ocean horizon. A lone man in a loose cream linen shirt stands ankle-deep at the shoreline, back to camera, arms slightly open. As the sun breaks the horizon, the sky above slowly opens into a gold and deep-navy cosmic nebula, and an eight-pointed star of light forms exactly where the sun meets the water. Slow dolly-in from behind, anamorphic lens flare, soft 35mm film grain, gentle wind in the shirt and hair. Warm gold (#c9a24b) and cream (#e8e2d4) highlights against near-black (#0d0d10) shadows. Euphoric, nostalgic, free. Clean frame, text-free, single continuous shot, 8 seconds.

2–6s: what you did today toward it (studio, gym, show, email)
concepts.caption: Day 1. Write it down so you can't take it back.
concepts.why: Turns daily life into a story with a finish line. Followers come back to see the next day.

beats: 2–5s: sun breaks as the drop hits
5–10s: you on the beach / rooftop, eyes closed
concepts.caption: Start the day like this or don't start it at all.
concepts.why: Owns the morning, which no techno artist does. Instantly recognisable when repeated.

concepts.why: Comments are the strongest signal you can send the algorithm, and you get free A/B data on your music.

rules.d: If the first 2 seconds don't stop the thumb, nothing else exists.
A series you repeat 30 times beats 30 good ideas posted once.
People follow where you're going, not where you've been.
Your vault is a test lab. Let the data pick the next single.
When a post works, post it again with a new hook. Don't retire it.
A 70% post today teaches you more than a 100% post that never ships.

trials.d: Trial Reels go to non-followers first. Your followers don't see them unless they perform.
Same clip, 2 different hooks, both as Trials. Keep the winner.
Every Vault Roulette snippet and every Savior teaser goes through Trials first.
You stop guessing. Bad tests never touch your grid, so you can test without fear.
